title: Needed, But What Does It Say?

scenes.tts: Removal shows that a signal is needed. Can it show what the signal says?
scenes.visual: Title card: Needed, But What Does It Say?
scenes.narration: Removal shows that a signal is needed. Can it show what the signal says?

scenes.tts: The fuel in a car is needed for the trip. But it does not choose where the car goes.
scenes.visual: A car with a fuel gauge on a road that forks; the driver, not the fuel, picks the fork.
scenes.narration: The fuel in a car is needed for the trip. But it does not choose where the car goes.

scenes.tts: A permissive signal allows an outcome that something else chooses. An instructive signal chooses the outcome itself.
scenes.visual: Two cards: permissive, allows an outcome that something else chooses; instructive, chooses the outcome itself.
scenes.narration: A permissive signal allows an outcome that something else chooses. An instructive signal chooses the outcome itself.

scenes.tts: Removing a signal cannot tell the two apart. One test of a spatial message: keep the signal present, but change where it is.
scenes.visual: The cortex schematic; the Reelin source slides from the top to other positions.
scenes.narration: Removing a signal cannot tell the two apart. One test of a spatial message: keep the signal present, but change where it is.

scenes.tts: Three simple proposals: stop here, let go of the glial fiber, or come here.
scenes.visual: Three icons: a stop sign; a hand letting go of a fiber; an arrow pointing toward a source.
scenes.narration: Three simple proposals: stop here, let go of the glial fiber, or come here.

scenes.tts: Now move the Reelin: below the cortex, into one small spot, or into the medium bathing a slice.
scenes.visual: Three panels: Reelin from below at the ventricular zone; Reelin in one spot; a slice sitting in a bath of Reelin-containing medium (no concentrations drawn inside the tissue).
scenes.narration: Now move the Reelin: below the cortex, into one small spot, or into the medium bathing a slice.

scenes.tts: Predict. If Reelin means come here, what should happen in each case?
scenes.visual: Predict card over the three panels.
scenes.narration: Predict. If Reelin means come here, what should happen in each case?

scenes.tts: In two thousand two, Curran's laboratory made Reelin from the ventricular zone of reeler mice.
scenes.caption: In 2002, Curran's laboratory made Reelin from the ventricular zone of reeler mice.
scenes.visual: Credit: Curran laboratory, 2002. Panel 1 lights up: Reelin made below the cortex.
scenes.narration: In 2002, Curran's laboratory made Reelin from the ventricular zone of reeler mice.

scenes.tts: The preplate split, and the ataxia was rescued, though not every defect. Neurons did not migrate down toward the source.
scenes.visual: Panel 1 result: the preplate splits; neurons do not turn down. A cross on the come-here arrow.
scenes.narration: The preplate split, and the ataxia was rescued, though not every defect. Neurons did not migrate down toward the source.

scenes.tts: In twenty ten, Nakajima's laboratory made Reelin in one small patch of mouse cortex.
scenes.caption: In 2010, Nakajima's laboratory made Reelin in one small patch of mouse cortex.
scenes.visual: Credit: Nakajima laboratory, 2010. Panel 2 lights up.
scenes.narration: In 2010, Nakajima's laboratory made Reelin in one small patch of mouse cortex.

scenes.tts: Later-born neurons passed earlier-born ones toward the spot, building a small inside-out arrangement around it.
scenes.visual: Panel 2 result: coloured neurons form a ball around the spot, latest-born nearest the centre.
scenes.narration: Later-born neurons passed earlier-born ones toward the spot, building a small inside-out arrangement around it.

scenes.tts: In two thousand four, Jossin, Goffinet and colleagues added Reelin to the medium bathing reeler slices.
scenes.caption: In 2004, Jossin, Goffinet and colleagues added Reelin to the medium bathing reeler slices.
scenes.visual: Credit: Jossin, Goffinet and colleagues, 2004. Panel 3 lights up.
scenes.narration: In 2004, Jossin, Goffinet and colleagues added Reelin to the medium bathing reeler slices.

scenes.tts: The developing cortical plate became more organized, without Reelin from its normal source. Whether Reelin stayed even inside the tissue was not shown.
scenes.visual: Panel 3 result: a more orderly cortical plate in a short-term slice assay. Small label: tissue distribution not measured.
scenes.narration: The developing cortical plate became more organized, without Reelin from its normal source. Whether Reelin stayed even inside the tissue was not shown.

scenes.tts: No single command fits all three results.
scenes.visual: The three panels with ticks and crosses for each simple proposal.
scenes.narration: No single command fits all three results.

scenes.tts: When does a neuron read Reelin? Follow a typical later-born neuron. First it is multipolar, wandering below the cortical plate.
scenes.visual: A timeline labelled: a typical later-born neuron. One neuron with several short processes drifting in the intermediate zone. Label: multipolar.
scenes.narration: When does a neuron read Reelin? Follow a typical later-born neuron. First it is multipolar, wandering below the cortical plate.

scenes.tts: Then it takes hold of a radial glial fiber, and climbs.
scenes.visual: The neuron grips a radial glial fiber and climbs.
scenes.narration: Then it takes hold of a radial glial fiber, and climbs.

scenes.tts: Near the top, it anchors its leading process in the marginal zone and pulls its cell body up: somal translocation.
scenes.visual: The neuron releases the fiber, anchors its leading process in the marginal zone, and pulls up. Label: somal translocation.
scenes.narration: Near the top, it anchors its leading process in the marginal zone and pulls its cell body up: somal translocation.

scenes.tts: Reelin signalling, through Dab one and Rap one, has been linked to both the turn and that final step.
scenes.caption: Reelin signalling, through Dab1 and Rap1, has been linked to both the turn and that final step.
scenes.visual: Two steps on the timeline glow: turning the multipolar neuron (N-cadherin adhesion), and somal translocation.
scenes.narration: Reelin signalling, through Dab1 and Rap1, has been linked to both the turn and that final step.

scenes.tts: On one view, Reelin acts less like a command, and more like a switch on adhesion, flipped at particular stages.
scenes.visual: A switch icon appears at each of the two steps. Label: one view.
scenes.narration: On one view, Reelin acts less like a command, and more like a switch on adhesion, flipped at particular stages.

scenes.tts: The essential cue, a gradient, a boundary or an adhesive state, is not settled.
scenes.visual: Three faint options on screen: gradient, boundary, adhesive state. Label: open question.
scenes.narration: The essential cue, a gradient, a boundary or an adhesive state, is not settled.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: Reelin signalling helps each new wave tend to finish its climb at the top. That alone does not show that neurons steer toward Reelin.
scenes.visual: Closing card, calling back to chapter 1: neurons are born in order; Reelin signalling is needed to stack that order the right way up. Below it, the takeaway as narrated: Reelin signalling helps each new wave tend to finish its climb at the top; that alone does not show that neurons steer toward Reelin.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: Reelin signalling helps each new wave tend to finish its climb at the top. That alone does not show that neurons steer toward Reelin.
